reference.title: Sitting Scapula Adduction (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you squeeze, breathe normally through the hold, breathe in as you release.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s in, 3 s hold, 1 s out

prescription.progression: Longer holds (5-10 s); prone or band versions

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a bench, feet flat. Elbows bent about 90 degrees and a little out from the sides, palms facing in, shoulders relaxed and down.
Breathe out and squeeze the shoulder blades back and together; the elbows travel back a little.
Hold about 3 s; neck long, chest proud but ribs down, no shrug.

mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears; squeeze back, not up.
Keep the ribs down; move only the shoulder blades.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the elbows back without moving the shoulder blades
mistakes.fix: Think of pinching a pencil between the shoulder blades.
Keep the head stacked over the shoulders.

kinematics.norm: With 45 degrees of abduction and the elbow bent 90 degrees, the clavicle retracted about 15 degrees from neutral stance (prone, Oyama 2010)
Elbows bent about 90 degrees, upper arms a little out from the sides (Oyama 2010 exercise 5 used 45 degrees of abduction)
Upright and still on the bench (clinical opinion)
About 1 s in, 3 s hold, 1 s out (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #691312, Sitting Scapula Adduction (male), video (movement reference)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Oyama 2010 tested prone exercises in healthy young adults; seated values are inferred.
modify: Neck tension: let the arms hang and only squeeze the shoulder blades.
Low back aches when sitting: sit with the back against a wall or the bench pad upright.
progressions: Band pull-aparts or seated band rows.

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades back toward the spine. In prone retraction exercises the middle trapezius reached up to about 77% of maximal activity with the arms raised (Oyama 2010); the rhomboids could not be measured with surface EMG.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades back toward the spine. In prone retraction exercises the middle trapezius reached up to about 77% of maximal activity with the arms raised (Oyama 2010); the rhomboids could not be measured with surface EMG.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Draws the elbows back as the shoulder blades squeeze.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Draws the elbows back as the shoulder blades squeeze.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the upper arms turned out slightly.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the upper arms turned out slightly.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the upper back tall so the squeeze comes from the shoulder blades, not an arch.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the upper back tall so the squeeze comes from the shoulder blades, not an arch.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the low back neutral.

guides.label: Elbows travel back as the blades squeeze
